title: Network Adequacy Standards and Time-Distance Requirements
summary: Details federal and state network adequacy requirements for Medicaid MCOs, including the 2024 Access rule's new appointment wait time standards and provider-to-enrollee ratios.
objectives: Describe the federal network adequacy framework under 42 CFR §438.68
Explain time-and-distance standards and how states set them
Identify the 2024 Access rule's new appointment wait time requirements

content_blocks.body:
42 CFR §438.68 requires states to set a quantitative network adequacy standard (such as time-and-distance or provider-to-enrollee ratios) for specified provider types and, since the 2024 rule, appointment wait time standards. States must establish standards for at least the following provider types: primary care (adult and pediatric), OB/GYN, mental health and substance use disorder (adult and pediatric), specialist, hospital, pharmacy, and pediatric dental.

The 2024 Managed Care Access, Finance, and Quality rule (89 FR 41002) strengthened these requirements substantially, adding mandatory appointment wait time standards and requiring states to conduct secret shopper surveys to validate compliance.

content_blocks.body: A longstanding problem in Medicaid managed care is 'ghost networks' — provider directories listing doctors who are not actually accepting Medicaid patients. The 2024 Access rule requires states to conduct secret shopper surveys to test whether listed providers are actually available to enrollees. This addresses a gap where MCOs could meet network adequacy standards on paper while enrollees faced access barriers in practice.
